scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: The Priorities list orders Discovery Readiness (P3) before Metadata Stack Completeness (P4), but the 'At a Glance' table narrative lists them in reverse order: 'Structured Data Quality at 65/100, Catalogue Visibility at 10/100, Metadata Stack Completeness at 49/100, and Discovery Readiness at 25/100', placing Metadata Stack before Discovery Readiness, contradicting the numbered priority order.
findings.context: Structured Data Quality at 65/100, Catalogue Visibility at 10/100, Metadata Stack Completeness at 49/100, and Discovery Readiness at 25/100

findings.message: The Machine Experience scorecard paragraph switches mid-section from third-person ('Machines can reliably process content') to first-person ('how consistently they can find and contextualise what we publish'), mixing voices within the same narrative paragraph.
findings.context: constrain how consistently they can find and contextualise what we publish

findings.message: The Summary of Findings section switches from third-person ('https://dkd.de performs at its strongest') to first-person ('We invite the team at https://dkd.de to review the findings') within the same paragraph.
findings.context: We invite the team at https://dkd.de to review the findings that follow

findings.message: The Security Headers section states '4 of the five standard security headers are absent across every audited response' but then asserts this as a site-wide fact — the prose says 'Adding these at the origin-server or CDN edge closes the corresponding attack surfaces' with no sample-scope qualifier, and the header table above it states all five headers as 'Yes' (present), directly contradicting the finding that four are absent.
findings.context: 4 of the five standard security headers are absent across every audited response: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS

findings.message: The 'At a Glance' findings table includes 'Catalogue Visibility at 10/100' as a named metric in the introductory narrative, but no Priority item in the numbered Priorities list (P1–P6) addresses Catalogue Visibility, meaning it appears in the findings summary without a corresponding priority.
findings.context: Structured Data Quality at 65/100, Catalogue Visibility at 10/100, Metadata Stack Completeness at 49/100

No issue here — re-examining the actual gap: the What's Next table's 'Critical Fixes' phase is scoped to 'P1, P2 (Compliance Risk)' only, which correctly excludes P3-P6.
